北京炸酱面

Beijing Zhajiangmian · Soybean Paste Noodles

Prompt

Premium Chinese restaurant food poster featuring deconstructed layers of 北京炸酱面 / Beijing Zhajiangmian / Soybean Paste Noodles floating in a vertical stack on pure black background. Seven distinct layers from top to bottom, including a large empty gap before the finished dish. Upper layers are RAW, UNCOOKED recipe ingredients; only the final dish at the bottom is cooked.

1) Top layer: a crisp floating cluster of raw pale scallion whites, fresh green scallion segments, ivory garlic slices and a few pale ginger slices. These aromatics are uncooked, with fresh clean cut surfaces and no caramelization.

2) Second layer: small fresh RAW pork belly dice, clearly showing alternating pale pink meat and creamy white fat. Clean cut edges and a natural moist sheen, without browned surfaces, caramelized crust, cooked sauce or steam.

3) Third layer: a loosely coiled nest of uncooked fresh wheat noodles, pale ivory with long distinct strands, a lightly flour-dusted matte surface and firm dough texture. These are RAW noodles before boiling; no glossy oil coating, cooked softness, sauce, egg-noodle yellow color or steam.

4) Fourth layer: fresh RAW cucumber matchsticks with dark green skin and translucent pale green centers, alongside crisp white and pale pink radish matchsticks. Keep the julienned vegetables clean, bright and uncooked, with no cooked sauce or oil coating.

5) Fifth layer: a transparent glass bowl containing two side-by-side dollops of unheated thick fermented yellow soybean paste (huangjiang), golden-brown, and sweet bean paste (tianmianjiang), deep brown. Show dense smooth paste texture and subtle gloss. These are the condiments before frying, not finished meat sauce: no pork pieces, cooked bits, boiling bubbles, red chili oil or steam in this bowl.

6) Sixth layer: EMPTY SPACE - a generous gap with only a few tiny flour particles and subtle steam rising from the completed hot noodles below. No spice cloud, dried chilies or unrelated ingredients.

7) Bottom/Final layer: a complete cooked 北京炸酱面 / Beijing Zhajiangmian in a dark brown ceramic bowl, at the same 45-degree viewing angle as the upper layers. Show a generous nest of boiled pale ivory wheat noodles, topped with glossy thick deep brown fried soybean-paste sauce containing browned diced pork. Arrange fresh green cucumber and crisp pale radish matchsticks in distinct neat clusters on top, with a little chopped scallion. Some visible noodle strands are lightly coated in the dark meat sauce while the brown sauce remains concentrated on top. Subtle steam rises from the hot noodles. This is a Beijing soybean-paste noodle dish: no red Sichuan chili broth, curry gravy, coconut milk, peanuts, peas, tofu or chicken.

Chinese and English annotation pairs, in ingredient order:
"葱姜蒜" / "Scallion, Ginger & Garlic"
"生猪肉丁" / "Raw Diced Pork"
"生鲜面条" / "Uncooked Wheat Noodles"
"黄瓜与萝卜" / "Cucumber & Radish"
"黄酱与甜面酱" / "Soybean & Sweet Bean Paste"
"成品" / "Finished Dish"

Each of the five ingredient layers floats freely with normal spacing. After the fifth layer, leave an intentional empty transition space two to three times larger than an ordinary gap. At the bottom, reveal the complete cooked dish in a traditional dark brown ceramic bowl. Use the same 45-degree camera angle and consistent scale and dramatic studio lighting throughout. All upper ingredient layers must look RAW or UNCOOKED AS USED BEFORE THIS RECIPE IS COOKED: plain pink meat, fresh crisp vegetables, unheated condiments and spices, and uncooked noodles where specified. No cooked crust, browned meat, stir-fried vegetables, finished meat sauce, or steam in the upper layers. Fermented pastes and tofu are shown as recipe ingredients before pan cooking.

Set everything against pure black (#000000), with warm rim lighting, realistic glass reflections, rich food textures, luxurious commercial restaurant photography and a 9:16 portrait format. Keep the ingredients centered. Place legible warm cream bilingual labels around them, alternating left and right, with thin elegant curved arrows. Chinese appears above English; render only the specified labels, once each, with generous margins and no overlap with food. The empty transition gap has no label. Only the finished dish emits subtle steam, rising into the transition gap. Add a few drifting spice particles appropriate to this dish and a small star sparkle at the bottom right beside the finished bowl. All layers float freely: no table, pedestal, platform, plate under the ingredients, extra title, logo, slogan or unrelated food.
